play_info.title: So the Path Does Not Die
play_info.author: Pede Hollist

summary.overview: So the Path Does Not Die is a contemporary Nigerian play by Pede Hollist, a leading voice in contemporary African drama. It explores themes of identity, family loyalty, tradition versus modernity, and the moral cost of silence. The play follows the story of a young man who returns home to confront the secrets of his father’s past during the Nigerian Civil War era. It is widely studied in Nigerian secondary schools as a text on the weight of history, reconciliation, and the importance of speaking truth.
summary.plot_summary: The play is set in a small Nigerian village and centres on two generations. The young protagonist, Chukwudi, returns home after years in the city and discovers that his father, a retired civil servant who fought in the Biafran War, has been living a double life. Chukwudi learns that his father was involved in a secret relationship and that his mother was forced to leave the family. Through tense family confrontations, Chukwudi learns that his father killed a man during the war to protect his family and has been carrying the guilt ever since. The play ends with the father confessing everything to Chukwudi, who in turn chooses to break the cycle of silence by forgiving and moving forward. The title ‘So the Path Does Not Die’ refers to the importance of carrying the past forward without letting it destroy the present.
